Adjacent evaluations are useful when they isolate a capability that the Million
LLMs task also needs. They are not alternate editions of the same leaderboard.
Their candidate pools, evidence available at decision time, labels, metrics, and
optimization targets define distinct evaluation contracts.

## What each neighboring family can teach

**Routing evaluations.** RouterBench exposes a query-by-model performance matrix
for learning query-dependent selection, while LLMRouterBench compares routing
methods under a unified protocol and highlights the importance of simple
baselines. RouteLLM uses preference data to learn a cost-aware router. These
evaluations support complementarity features, pairwise supervision, and
baseline discipline. They commonly select among fewer real models and may
optimize cost, rather than produce a full ordering of 150 fixed IDs.

**Retrieval benchmarks.** BEIR evaluates zero-shot information retrieval across
heterogeneous domains, and MTEB compares embedding behavior over many tasks.
They justify testing sparse and dense retrieval together and warn that no
encoder dominates every domain. Their scores cannot choose a TREC router:
retrieving documents or embedding pairs is an upstream capability, not the
track's candidate-ranking outcome.

**Answer and judge evaluations.** MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena helped establish
pairwise LLM judging and human preference comparisons. Subsequent primary work
documents order bias, verbosity bias, and evaluator self-preference. Those
findings motivate blinded candidates, reversed answer order, multiple judges,
criterion-specific rubrics, and preserved disagreements when creating weak
labels. They do not turn an LLM judge's vote into an official qrel.

**Distribution-shift evaluations.** WILDS and shift-detection research make the
evaluation boundary explicit: average in-distribution validation can conceal
failures on changed topics or sources. For this task, query-cluster holdouts and
slice analysis are robustness checks, not substitutes for the organizer's
hidden set.

## Comparability rule

Borrow the evaluation design or evidence signal, then recreate it within the
current 150-candidate, no-test-time-call protocol. Never compare an external
benchmark's quality, accuracy, preference rate, or cost saving directly with
TREC nDCG@10 or MRR. Only same-data, same-split, same-metric development runs
belong in local method comparisons.

## Deep dive

Start with [RouterBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12031),
[BEIR](https://datasets-benchmarks-proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2021/hash/65b9eea6e1cd2a47751a186f-Abstract-round2.html),
and [WILDS](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v139/koh21a.html) for the routing,
retrieval, and shift contracts. The full audited registry remains at
`reports/trec_2026_approaches_guide.artifact.json` for repository agents.
